舞殿宮"...Chief. This is certain? No room for a mistake?"
Chief"...Unfortunately, Highness. Several separate channels have brought me the same information."
Chief"At the Oyumi Kubo's headquarters, preparations for a major military operation have begun."
舞殿宮"And the target...?"
Chief"Nothing has been announced. But taking the present situation into account... most likely..."
舞殿宮"Yes. Not much mystery left there."
Chief"...Only their slow preparations are in our favor. They cannot judge our strength, I suspect."
Chief"We still have time to take some action."
舞殿宮"...Even so, Chief."
Chief"..."
舞殿宮"My luck, it seems, has finally said bas. Enough."
Chief"No, Highness. Kyoto remains. Even the shogunate cannot send its soldiers into the Imperial Palace."
Chief"I shall arrange your departure from Kamakura immediately—"
舞殿宮"That will not do, Kikuchi..."
Chief"...Highness."
舞殿宮"If I withdraw now, there is no coming back. As Prince Maidono, I am finished..."
舞殿宮"Politically dead, but keeping myself alive? After all this plotting, I should take no responsibility at all? That is a very ugly way to survive."
Chief"But—"
舞殿宮"I have some shame left. So have you."
舞殿宮"On that battlefield, remembering it was the one thing that kept us humanhuman. Was it not?"
Chief"Highness..."
ｅｔｃ／十傑Ａ"An admirable resolve. Then permit me to grant you an honorable death, Your Highness Prince Haruhiro of Maidono."
Chief"What—"
舞殿宮"Who is there!?"

Her clear voice silenced every objection at last.

I had no reply. Things needed saying. Against this reckless faith of hers, surely I had something to say.

Nothing came. I was <ruby>overwhelmed<rt>overwhelmed</rt></ruby>. The prince and chief appeared no better off.

This was not the Ichijou I had known. Not even yesterday's girl, trembling at the horror of killing a man.

Before, she had possessed only a will. To carry justice through. Never to forgive those who used violence to trample the weak.

A child's weightless dream: no grounds for it, no means of making it real.

Now she was different.

She had confidence. The certainty that she could destroy evil. The pride of knowing her blade could judge even the mighty wicked, arrogant in their power and beyond the reach of law.

She had defeated Doushin Yusa. By sheer <ruby>force of will<rt>power</rt></ruby>, she had crossed even her terror at that killing.

And the girl had been reborn—<ruby>as an executioner of justice<rt>・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>.

Ichijou Ayane had finally become what she had wished to be.

The one called Kuronose Douji wore black military dress covering his whole body. I could not make out his face. The princess's younger brother must still be young; from his build, perhaps twenty or so.

He too was studying us. One look was enough for the gloomy-faced man. Having measured me, his attention moved on.

The earnest girl beside me received a very different look. Respect from the beginning. Her slight frame, so unlike a warrior's, seemed to increase it.

To have accomplished that, in such a small body. His sigh and lowered gaze said as much. His eyes were <ruby>filled<rt>filled</rt></ruby> with something close to worship.

—Something was wrong.

Something was not right.

No... was it me? Somehow, <ruby>they<rt>・・</rt></ruby> felt far away.

One will was <ruby>drawing together<rt>drawing together</rt></ruby> this room. I alone remained awake.

...My wandering gaze caught the assassin's corpse. Long since dead, it was beginning to stiffen.

Cut in two with a single stroke. No hesitation in that blade.

Ichijou would hesitate no longer. She would keep fighting, without doubt.

Princess Sakurako, Kuronose Douji, the chief, the prince... the same will was in them all. Fight. No doubt about it.

Was I alone in hesitating?

No. I had no reason to. With Ichijou's help, the curse would not bind me.

I had brought about Doushin Yusa's death, yes. But no life had been demanded in payment. I had killed no good person.

The relief of that went deep.

Then... what was wrong?

Raichou Imagawa was no innocent either. In the Osaka massacre, foremost among Rokuhara's crimes, he had reportedly commanded the Umeda district. Burned the whole area with its residents inside it. Taken thousands of lives.

Ichijou said he deserved death. I could only agree. No defense came to mind; I had no wish to make one.

Then where was the problem? Beside Ichijou and the prince, what reason had I not to fight?

—Something was wrong.

Something was not right.

No... was it me? Somehow, they・・ felt far away.

One will was drawing togetherdrawing together this room. I alone remained awake.

...My wandering gaze caught the assassin's corpse. Long since dead, it was beginning to stiffen.

Cut in two with a single stroke. No hesitation in that blade.

Ichijou would hesitate no longer. She would keep fighting, without doubt.

Princess Sakurako, Kuronose Douji, the chief, the prince... the same will was in them all. Fight. No doubt about it.

Was I alone in hesitating?

No. I had no reason to. With Ichijou's help, the curse would not bind me.

I had brought about Doushin Yusa's death, yes. But no life had been demanded in payment. I had killed no good person.

The relief of that went deep.

Then... what was wrong?

Raichou Imagawa was no innocent either. In the Osaka massacre, foremost among Rokuhara's crimes, he had reportedly commanded the Umeda district. Burned the whole area with its residents inside it. Taken thousands of lives.

Ichijou said he deserved death. I could only agree. No defense came to mind; I had no wish to make one.

Then where was the problem? Beside Ichijou and the prince, what reason had I not to fight?

I did not imagine a paradise waiting at the end. But the prince would surely make Yamato easier to live in than Rokuhara did. Easier than under GHQ's occupation.

Was that wrong?

The opposite.

Justice was here. Here was a justice one could believe in.

So fight for it. Was that not enough?

However much I fought, however many evil people I killed, I no longer needed to kill the good・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・.
